items.author: ziangit
items.summary: Scheduler now preserves and forwards the timeout finished_reason through chunked-prefill aborts so clients receive HTTP 503 instead of a generic 200 abort.
items.body:
## Motivation

When `SGLANG_REQ_RUNNING_TIMEOUT` is set and a request times out while decoding, the client gets HTTP 503 with `Request running timeout reached.` If the same timeout hits while the request is still in chunked prefill, the client gets HTTP 200 with `finish_reason = {"type": "abort", "message": "Abort in waiting queue"}`. So a client that retries on 503 won't retry it, and it doesn't show up as a timeout.

items.author: BugenZhao
items.summary: Binds env-only settings to hidden typed flags in the Rust frontend so unimplemented values fail startup explicitly instead of being silently dropped.

## Overview

The Python frontend reads several settings only from environment variables (`vllm.envs`); the Rust frontend ignored the ones below, so a deployment that set one silently lost its effect. This PR binds each as a hidden typed flag, as vllm-project/vllm#68841 did for the first env-only settings, and declares in the flag's type which values the Rust frontend implements, so any other value fails startup on both `vllm-rs serve` and the Python-launched `--args-json` path.

items.author: zhangjiaohao
items.summary: Fixes GDN convolution-state corruption when NGRAM emits tree-structured sibling proposals by allocating independent per-node convolution windows instead of overlapping storage that allows siblings to overwrite accepted checkpoints.
items.body:
## Motivation

NGRAM may emit sibling nodes even at BFS breadth one. Hybrid linear attention currently uses EAGLE top-k to select verify metadata, and the Mamba pool uses top-k to select its convolution scratch layout. Overlapping windows work for a chain. In a tree, a sibling can overwrite an accepted node's convolution window before commit.

For example, start with history `[1, 2, 3]`, root `4`, and three sibling proposals `5`, `6`, and `7`. The root checkpoint must be `[2, 3, 4]`. With overlapping storage, the observed root checkpoint is `[2, 3, 3]`.

Adds a second lookup backend for Engram tables that are row-sharded over DP x CP (`--engram-parallel-size`): a symmetric GIN/LSA device transport, ported from #7224. Inside an NVLink (LSA) domain a requester reads the owner's registered table rows directly; across domains, requests, rows and gradients travel over GPU-initiated networking (GIN). `--engram-communication-backend {symmetric,nccl}` selects the backend, and `symmetric` becomes the default for row groups of more than one rank.

items.author: haoyangli0109
items.summary: sgl-kernel's ROCm QuickReduce reduces bf16 in fp16 by default, and fp16 tops out at 65504. For the FP codec, guards that ceiling with a power-of-two prescale: it divides by S = 16 before the fp16 cast and multiplies back on output.
items.body:
## Motivation

sgl-kernel's ROCm QuickReduce reduces bf16 in fp16 by default (`ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_CAST_BF16_TO_FP16=1`), and fp16 tops out at 65504. For the FP codec, `main` guards that ceiling with a power-of-two prescale: it divides by S = 16 before the fp16 cast and multiplies back on output. That only moves fp16's window up by 16x, so both ends of the bf16 range still go wrong:

- Sums above 16 × 65504 (about 1.05e6) are clamped.
- Values below about 1e-4 fall into fp16's subnormal range after the division and lose mantissa bits; below about 5e-7 they become zero.

Both errors are silent: F

items.body:
## Motivation

The Marlin MoE JIT module builds the kernels of every weight type it supports, whatever the caller quantized with. In BF16 that is 204 `Marlin<...>` instances (uint4, uint4b8, uint8b128, NVFP4, MXFP4, three FP8 flavours and act-order), while a model uses one or two of these types. On a cold start this one module is the slowest JIT build: about 4 minutes on 1x H200, inside the first prefill CUDA graph capture. Inkling 2's Hopper experts (NVFP4 and FP8), the `marlin` MoE runner (the Hopper default for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash's NVFP4 experts) and GPTQ/AWQ MoE models all go through it.

items.body:
LPM and other cache-aware prefill policies match waiting requests against the KV cache, then use a second temporary tree to identify requests that should wait for a shared prefix. For each cold leader the scheduler allocates a dummy tensor and inserts the truncated key into the second tree. Since [#46022](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46022), keys in that second pass are limited to the defer threshold. A partial match below the threshold never changes the decision.

items.author: alphabetc1
items.summary: builds the decode batch for HiSparse requests leaving staging, and with it sets to each request's prompt. The normal path uses the request's own.
items.body:
## Motivation

`Scheduler._build_hisparse_decode_batch` builds the decode batch for HiSparse requests leaving staging, and with `return_logprob` it sets `token_ids_logprobs` to each request's prompt (`origin_input_ids`). The normal path uses the request's own `token_ids_logprob`. So a HiSparse request that asks for `token_ids_logprob=[...]` gets, at every decode step, logprobs for the prompt's token ids instead of the ones it asked for; a request that asks for none still gathers a prompt-length id list per step.

## Modifications

- Use `r.logprob.token_ids_logprob`, as the normal decode path

items.title: [Perf] diffusion/magi2: Run the adapters on each rank's own rows
items.author: mickqian
items.summary: Eliminates redundant full-sequence all-gather and fp32 GEMM under sequence parallelism in MAGI-2 by restricting each rank's adapter work to its local rows, shrinking communication to 112-channel projections.
items.body:
## Motivation

Under sequence parallelism, every MAGI-2 rank runs the fp32 input adapter over the whole packed sequence, then keeps only its own shard. At the end of each forward it all-gathers the full residual stream, which is 4 × 3072 channels wide, only to project it down to 112 output channels. The adapters are per-row, so every rank but one throws that work away. For a preview forward at the default 896×512, 10 s clip, that is about 115k rows: a 2.8 GB all-gather, a 5.6 GB fp32 copy, and the fp32 embedding and projection GEMMs, all repeated on every rank in every forward. ## Motivation

items.title: [Fix] [NPU] Hicache: support layer-first split MLA pages in Mooncake L3
items.author: dqh1900013087-tech
items.summary: On Ascend, GLM-5.2 can use to move its MLA cache between the NPU and host memory. With Mooncake L3 enabled, the host pool registered only the K buffer, and raised when asked for a storage page.
items.body:
## Motivation

On Ascend, GLM-5.2 can use `layer_first_kv_split` to move its MLA cache between the NPU and host memory. With Mooncake L3 enabled, the host pool registered only the K buffer, and `get_page_buffer_meta()` raised `ValueError: Unsupported layout: layer_first_kv_split` when asked for a storage page.

This PR enables Mooncake to back up and restore these pages with `DCP=1`.

## Modifications

- Register every nonempty host buffer used by a split MLA page, including the RoPE buffer, indexer keys, and indexer scales when present. Packed FP8 pages already carry RoPE in the K buf

items.title: [Bugfix][Model Loader] Layerwise reload: start over after a reload that raised
items.author: hallerite
items.summary: Discards stale buffered tensors from a failed layerwise reload so the next retry reinstalls every weight instead of silently leaving zeroed values on the meta device.
items.body:
## Overview

A layerwise weight reload that raises partway leaves layers on the meta device with their buffered weights, and the next `initialize_layerwise_reload` skips those layers as already initialized. A retried update then reports success while installing stale or zeroed weights. With this change, `initialize_layerwise_reload` first restores the live tensors of any layer an unfinished reload left behind and drops what that reload buffered, so the retry starts over. This complements #57854, which adds `abort_layerwise_reload` to the failure paths of vLLM's own weight-transfer engines.

items.summary: Fixes AttributeError in layerwise model reload by replacing direct `loader.__name__` access with `getattr(loader, "__name__", None)`, unblocking reload for partial-based weight loaders like MiniMax-M2's q/k norms.

## Overview

Layerwise weight reload recognizes its own loader wrapper by `loader.__name__`. It therefore raises `AttributeError` for any weight loader without a `__name__`, such as a `functools.partial`. This change reads the name with `getattr(loader, "__name__", None)` at both places that check it.

items.body:
## Description

With chunked prefill disabled, a recompute-paused request is prefilled in one step with its prompt plus the tokens it had already generated. When that is more than `max_num_tokens`, `BudgetTracker.can_fit_tokens()` is never true, so the V2 scheduler's context loop returned STOP on that request every iteration. The request stayed at the head of the queue and no request behind it was scheduled again.

The scheduler now fails that one request with an error that names the cause, through the existing `take_lost_kv_requests()` path, and returns SKIP so the requests behind it keep run

## Motivation

MAGI-2-preview encodes every prompt with its 27B Qwen3.5 text encoder on the CPU, which takes 20-28 s per request on a 4x B200 server, about 7% of a 1080p clip. This PR runs that forward on the GPU, streaming the encoder's layers from pinned host memory, so the text stage drops to under a second without making the encoder resident on any GPU.

The forward was on the CPU for a reason: resident, the encoder would hold about 48 GB on every rank on top of both DiTs, and staging the whole model onto a card per request spikes device memory. Streaming its layers avoids both.

items.title: [KV Offload] Prefetch hinted prefixes into the GPU KV cache
items.author: liteboy-bit
items.summary: A request that knows it will reuse a prefix can carry that prefix's block hashes in its KV-hint envelope (#53421 / #53423). Today that hint is only consumed by the request's own lookup, so the CPU-tier load starts when the request is scheduled - on its critica…
items.body:
## Overview

A request that knows it will reuse a prefix can carry that prefix's block hashes in its KV-hint envelope (#53421 / #53423). Today that hint is only consumed by the request's own lookup, so the CPU-tier load starts when the request is scheduled - on its critical path. This PR lets the **offloading connector** act on the hint before any request exists: reserve GPU blocks by hash, load into them, publish them under those hashes, so the arriving prompt sees an ordinary prefix-cache hit. One new envelope action, no request/connector protocol change.

MessageQueue.create_from_process_group picks local readers using in_the_same_node_as, which tests whether a rank can see the writer's shared memory. The local reader then connects over a ZMQ socket on 127.0.0.1, and loopback is scoped to a network namespace while shared memory is not. Two Pods on one host that share /dev/shm but have separate network namespaces therefore classify each other as local readers, connect to their own loopback, and wait forever in wait_until_ready.

Change, in shm_broadcast.py:
- _get_network_namespace_id() returns the inode of /proc/self/ns/net, or N

items.title: [fsdp] fix: reduce peak memory during log-prob temperature scaling
items.author: blessedcursed
items.summary: The dense FSDP training path divides the full logits tensor by temperature before computing token log-probabilities. With a large vocabulary, the extra buffer can take several GiB.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

The dense FSDP training path divides the full logits tensor by temperature before computing token log-probabilities. With a large vocabulary, the extra buffer can take several GiB.

Add an opt-in chunk size for single-sequence micro-batches on the eager path. Each block is scaled as its log-probabilities are computed, so the scaled temporary is bounded by the chunk size and the original logits stay intact. Paths that need the full logits for additional outputs keep their existing behavior.

### Test

- `python -m pytest -q tests/workers/test_fsdp_temperature_scaling_

items.title: [Bug][Perf] Decode batches above the largest captured CUDA graph run eagerly and the server stays in a slow state
items.author: brianosaurus
items.summary: On 24 GB GPUs (tp < 4) the decode CUDA graph range is 48, but defaults to a KV-derived value (4096 on a 4090). Decode batches above 48 run eagerly at about 15x the cost of a replay (31 ms vs 2 ms with LoRA), requests drain slower than they arrive, and the batc…
items.body:
## Summary

On 24 GB GPUs (tp < 4) the decode CUDA graph range is 48, but `max_running_requests` defaults to a KV-derived value (4096 on a 4090). Decode batches above 48 run eagerly at about 15x the cost of a replay (31 ms vs 2 ms with LoRA), requests drain slower than they arrive, and the batch stays above 48. **Under sustained load the server does not recover:** at 40 rps every request that waited over 1 s (110 of 500) got its first token only after arrivals stopped. CPU contention alone can trigger it at 20 rps.

Same mechanism as #33483 (closed without a fix); still on main `385262cabb`.

items.title: [Perf] multimodal: Single-flight token-space item preprocessing
items.author: ChihTsungLu
items.summary: The token-space processor checks the item feature cache before it loads and preprocesses media. When several requests for the same image miss at the same time, each one loads, preprocesses and writes the item.
items.body:
> **Draft, stacked on #48307.** The base branch is `rockdu-dev-mm-v2/15-item-feature-cache-write-once` (the head of #48307, at `c7ef1ff4a8`), so the diff shows only this change. It follows up on the token-space item feature cache work tracked in #43314.

## Motivation

The token-space processor checks the item feature cache before it loads and preprocesses media. When several requests for the same image miss at the same time, each one loads, preprocesses and writes the item. A burst of N identical cold requests therefore costs N loads, N preprocessings and N cache writes, where 1 would do.

items.title: [Fix] entrypoints: Write SIGQUIT handler messages without re-entering stderr
items.author: nkq232
items.summary: Logging from a SIGQUIT handler re-enters 's buffered writer if the signal lands while the main thread is writing to stderr. Python then raises. [Discussion: Thanks @YidaWeng Both gaps are real: dumprequestsbeforecrash still logs before the kill, and th]
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #53352.

Logging from a SIGQUIT handler re-enters `sys.stderr`'s buffered writer if the signal lands while the main thread is writing to stderr. Python then raises `RuntimeError: reentrant call inside <_io.BufferedWriter name='<stderr>'>`. That exception escapes the handler and replaces the child's real failure as the launcher's exit error, which makes start-up failures hard to diagnose.

## Modifications

- Add `write_stderr_signal_safe()` to `sglang.srt.utils.process`. It writes one line to fd 2 with `os.write`, bypassing `sys.stderr`'s buffer.
- Use it in the three SIGQ
discussion:
Thanks @YidaWeng   
Both gaps are real: dump_requests_before_crash() still logs before the kill, and the reap warning in _wait_for_reap_or_raise isn't guarded. Your follow-up (192ac951eb) looks good to me, including the partial-write loop.

## Motivation

The FA4 Split-KV combine launches a separate grid Z slice per request. For packed varlen queries, it currently sizes each slice from the total number of query rows in the batch. items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #53327.

`_load_image` decodes JPEG on the GPU with `decode_jpeg(..., device="cuda")`, which defaults to `ImageReadMode.UNCHANGED`. One 1x1 grayscale JPEG from any client is enough to trigger it. For Qwen-VL, the request fails during preprocessing. #42

items.author: liranschour
items.summary: Implements RFC #69928 for NIXL pull: an opt-in that lets the decoder check, before using them, that the KV blocks it read hold the content it expects. Each producer block gets a 64 B metadata entry carrying its prefix-caching block hash; the decoder reads the …
items.body:
## Overview

Implements RFC #69928 for NIXL pull: an opt-in `kv_block_validation` (`off | log | enforce`) that lets the decoder check, before using them, that the KV blocks it read hold the content it expects. Each producer block gets a 64 B metadata entry carrying its prefix-caching block hash; the decoder reads the entries after the KV data and compares them with the hashes it computes from its own prompt.

## Motivation

In DeepSeek-V4.1 decode, the indexer's candidate source layer (layer 20) publishes 2048 candidate blocks of 8 positions per query row. The consumer layers (24/28/32/36) use these blocks as a mask, but they still score every position, building a dense `decode_mask` and then running `fp4_index_logits_paged`. At a 72K-token context only 16K of the 72K positions are candidates, so roughly 78% of the scoring work in these four layers is discarded.

Support the AngularMuOwn optimizer ([Muown Implicitly Performs Angular Step-size Decay](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23637)) for Muon matrices under MFSDP v2, end to end in Megatron-LM: optimizer, MCore integration, and checkpoints.

AngularMuOwn writes each row as `W_i = g_i U_i`. items.body:
## Problem

With `perf_metrics_output_dir` set, the disaggregated server should write one JSONL record for every request. For streaming requests, most records can be lost: clients disconnect as soon as they receive `data: [DONE]`, while the disaggregated record is appended only after the trailing performance-metrics event has been consumed. Under uvicorn's ASGI spec, Starlette cancels the streaming response on that disconnect before `on_resp_done` or the middleware's final-body path runs.

This supersedes #20280, rebasing the fix onto current main and addressing its remaining review findings.

items.title: [fsdp] fix: use actual chunk count for TiledMLP last-shard gradient write-back
items.author: four1er
items.summary: Fixes #8839 dropped parameter gradients accumulated by earlier micro-batches whenever returned fewer chunks than (e.g. moves any existing into its buffer and writes it back only from the hook installed with, and never fired in that case, so the accumulated gra…
items.body:
Fixes #8839

`TiledMLP.backward` dropped parameter gradients accumulated by earlier micro-batches whenever `torch.chunk` returned fewer chunks than `num_shards` (e.g. `n=9, shards=4` gives 3 chunks of 3). `GradientAccumulator` moves any existing `param.grad` into its buffer and writes it back only from the hook installed with `is_last_shard=True`, and `is_last_shard = i + 1 == shards` never fired in that case, so the accumulated gradients were silently lost.

This PR uses the actual chunk count (`len(x_shards)`) for the last-shard test, so the write-back hook always fires on the final shard.

items.title: [fsdp] TiledMLP drops accumulated gradients when torch.chunk returns fewer chunks than num_shards
items.author: elipskiy
items.summary: TiledMLP backward silently discards accumulated micro-batch gradients when torch.chunk yields fewer chunks than num_shards, leaving param.grad with only the final micro-batch's contribution.
items.body:
### What happens

`TiledMLP.backward` (`verl/models/transformers/tiled_mlp.py`) drops the parameter gradients that earlier micro-batches accumulated in `param.grad` whenever `torch.chunk` returns fewer chunks than `num_shards`.

`GradientAccumulator.__init__` moves any existing `param.grad` into its buffer and sets `param.grad = None`. The buffer is written back only by the hook installed with `is_last_shard=True`, and `is_last_shard = i + 1 == shards`. `torch.chunk(x, shards)` returns `ceil(n / ceil(n / shards))` chunks, which is fewer than `shards` for some `n` (for example `n = 9, shards =
discussion:

With verl's default mixed precision (`param_dtype=bf16`, `reduce_dtype=fp32`, `transformer_impl.py:396-402`) and deferred gradient sync on non-final micro-ba

Thanks for the detailed report and the CPU repro — I can reproduce this locally. I am working on a fix (use the actual chunk count for the last-shard hook) with a regression test, and will open a PR shortly.

### Feature request

For hybrid models (Qwen3.5, Qwen3-Next) on the SGLang rollout, hold each prompt's prefix state with an SGLang session (`--enable-session-radix-cache`, sglang >= 0.5.17, sgl-project/sglang#29173) until all samples of that prompt are done, then close the session.

### Motivation

A hybrid model can reuse a cached prefix only if the recurrent (Mamba) state at its end is still in SGLang's fixed-size state pool, which is evicted by LRU. With many prompts in flight, the prompts' states are the oldest and go first, so later samples of the same prompt recompute the whole prompt.

## What does this PR do?

Fix DSA split gradient norms in `FullyShardedOptimizer`, independently of Muon or optimizer CUDA graphs.

### What does this PR do?

When a TransferQueue put misses its data-status ACK (`TQ_DATA_UPDATE_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT`, 30s by default), TQ only logs it, so the controller never marks those samples ready. Rank 0 rewrote `latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt` with `open(..., 'w')` and `latest_train_state.pt` with `shutil.copy`, both in place, so a crash mid-save could leave an empty tracker behind. items.title: [TRTLLM-17824][fix] Release checkpoint keys as the DeepSeek-R1 Modeling V2 target loads
items.author: ruocheng-nv
items.summary: Releases checkpoint keys progressively during DeepSeek-R1 NVFP4 Modeling V2 load, cutting per-rank host memory from ~80 GB to ~26 GB and enabling online EPLB at reduced memory footprint.
items.body:
## Description

The DeepSeek-R1-0528 NVFP4 Modeling V2 target (`deepseek_v3/r1_0528_nvfp4__sm_10x__default`) held every checkpoint tensor it read until `load` returned. The engine's checkpoint dict can back many tensors with one read-ahead buffer, which is freed only when all of its keys are released, so every rank kept the checkpoint files it touched in host memory for the whole load: about 70-80 GB per rank at dep8 on GB300, where the built-in model holds about 26 GB.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/7094481][fix] Stop busy-polling in the trtllm-bench async client
items.author: chenfeiz0326
items.summary: Replaces busy-polling (asyncio.sleep(0)) with event-based waiting in trtllm-bench's async client to eliminate GIL contention that starved the LLM response-delivery thread on multi-socket hosts.
items.body:
## Description

trtllm-bench's async client dispatches its whole inbox into request tasks when the benchmark starts. For the rest of the run, `LlmManager.worker` then polled the empty inbox with `await asyncio.sleep(0)`, so the event loop never blocked: the client process kept a core busy and held the GIL most of the time. The LLM API thread that delivers each response to the request coroutines needs the GIL too.

On two-socket Intel hosts with Linux 5.15, like QA's H100 nodes, this starves that thread. CPython restarts a waiting thread's 5 ms switch timeout every time the GIL holder releases

## Problem

Static batch validation reports only the effective batch size and minimum batch size, without showing how they were derived.

For example, `train_batch_size=4`, `rollout.n=2`, and FSDP with 2 nodes × 3 devices produce:

Include the configured batch, rollout count, node/device counts, and backend-specific minimum-batch calculation, with guidance on which settings to adjust. Keep the validation rule unchanged.

items.title: [V1 FSDP] update_weights broadcasts full params every step (~9s/step on 32B); no delta or bucketed sync mode
items.author: dahai80
items.summary: On the V1 FSDP path, (actor → rollout engine weight sync) broadcasts the full parameter set every training step. Measured cost on Qwen2.5-32B TP8: ~9 s/step, every step, regardless of how few parameters changed.
items.body:
## Summary

On the V1 FSDP path, `update_weights` (actor → rollout engine weight sync) broadcasts the **full parameter set every training step**. Measured cost on Qwen2.5-32B TP8: ~9 s/step, every step, regardless of how few parameters changed. Over hundreds of GRPO steps this is a fixed tax proportional to model size, not to actual weight drift.

## Suggestion

A bucketed delta mode would remove most of this cost:

- hash/checksum per parameter bucket, sync only buckets whose checksum changed (in practice almost none change every step in RL fine-tuning — the update is small relative to init)

# What does this PR do?

Adds `lm_head_loss_num_chunks` (`--lm-head-loss-num-chunks`, default 1 = off). items.title: [trainer, worker, algo] fix: whiten advantages per mini-batch chunk in TrainingWorker
items.author: Doublrest
items.summary: In V1 trainers ( and ), whitens advantages once over the full sampled batch, whereas splits the batch into optimizer chunks without re-normalizing per chunk. When the sampled batch is larger than, individual optimizer chunks can have non-zero token-weighted ad…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8766.

In V1 trainers (`sync` and `colocate_async`), `_compute_advantage()` whitens advantages once over the full sampled batch, whereas `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()` splits the batch into `ppo_mini_batch_size` optimizer chunks without re-normalizing per chunk. When the sampled batch is larger than `ppo_mini_batch_size`, individual optimizer chunks can have non-zero token-weighted advantage means, introducing chunk-level policy-gradient drift.

This PR re-normalizes `mini_batch_td["advantages"]` per optimizer chunk in `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()`

items.summary: On verl v0.9.1, verl's own Qwen2-7B-Instruct GRPO GSM8K recipe (the baseline in ) crashed twice on 8x B200, both times on the first training step after a validation pass. Right before the crash, the agent-loop workers log and carry on.
items.body:
## Summary

On verl v0.9.1, verl's own Qwen2-7B-Instruct GRPO GSM8K recipe (the `qwen2-7b-fsdp2.log` baseline in `docs/algo/baseline.md`) crashed twice on 8x B200, both times on the first training step after a validation pass. Right before the crash, the agent-loop workers log `Timeout waiting for data status update ACK from controller after 30s` and carry on. The data was written to storage but the controller never marks it ready, so the trainer later gets an empty batch from TransferQueue and fails with `KeyError: 'loss_mask'` in `compute_log_prob`.

The timeout itself is a slow controller.

This adds an optional path that sends each data-parallel shard to exactly one model-parallel source rank and leaves redistribution to a worker-side preprocess hook. The worker does not create a model-parallel process group.

**Before:** `make_nd_compute_dataproto_dispatch_fn` always sent `arg[dp_rank]` to every worker on that data-parallel rank, and dispatch/collect metadata was a bare rank integer or bool.

**After:** Workers register `DispatchInfo(dp_rank, is_mp_src)`

items.title: [algo, trainer, fsdp, megatron, cfg, doc] feat: add topk_rb KL loss (top-k Rao-Blackwellised KL to the reference)
items.author: hiddevandebeek
items.summary: It adds, a KL penalty against the reference policy for. The estimator computes KL(πθ ‖ πref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Implements the RFC in #8536. It adds `actor.kl_loss_type: topk_rb`, a KL penalty against the reference policy for `use_kl_loss=True`.

The estimator computes KL(π_θ ‖ π_ref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket. The within-tail part is estimated from the sampled token, so the result is an **unbiased** estimate of the full-vocabulary KL gradient at every k, with much lower variance than the single-sample `kl`/`k2`/`low_var_kl`/`k3+` options. It is the per-token Rao-Blackwellised KL of [Amini et al., NeurIPS 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.1063

items.title: [vllm, rollout, perf] refactor: read sampled-token log-probs from flat lists
items.author: hxw12219
items.summary: Reads sampled-token log-probs from vLLM's flat lists instead of one dict per generated token, and makes the prompt log-prob reader work with flat lists. In a standalone AsyncLLM benchmark on one B300, rollout wall time fell from 6.99 s to 6.29 s (−10%).
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Reads sampled-token log-probs from vLLM's flat lists instead of one `Logprob` dict per generated token, and makes
the prompt log-prob reader work with flat lists. Outputs are unchanged. In a standalone AsyncLLM benchmark on one
B300, rollout wall time fell from 6.99 s to 6.29 s (−10%).

## Summary

When context compaction splits an episode into multiple training rows, `rollout/raw_reward` gives that episode extra weight. For example, four episodes with rewards `[1, 0, 0, 0]` report a mean of `0.25`. Splitting the first and last episodes into two rows each raises the logged mean to `0.3333`, even though the episode rewards are identical.

Compute the mean over episodes before data-parallel partitioning. Each episode contributes equally, including when its segments land on different ranks. In the example above, the logged mean stays at `0.25` after splitting.

Rank 0 creates the --save-hf directory and copies the non-weight files of --hf-checkpoint into it, then the

already exists on the server.

goes to the server and refreshes the cached entry; where the directory is already visible it does nothing.

items.title: [reward] fix: compare prime_code call-based outputs as plain builtins
items.author: Aarav500
items.summary: In, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of or whose always returns got full reward on every call-based task.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8656. In `prime_code`, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with `output == expected`. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of `int` or `list` whose `__eq__` always returns `True` got full reward on every call-based task. Swapping the operands doesn't help, because Python tries a subclass's reflected `__eq__` first.

This adds `_to_builtin()` in `prime_code/testing_util.py` and applies it to the output right after the existing `json.dumps(output)` call. It rebuilds the value from plain `None`/`bool`/`int`/`float

items.author: R0k1e

## Motivation

`Float16Module.forward` upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with `labels=None`, so the whole `[T, V]` logits tensor is copied to fp32. It is the largest single allocation in a long-context actor step: 40,960 tokens × 248,320 vocabulary is about 41 GB in fp32 versus 20 GB in bf16.

items.body:
## Problem

With `--partial-rollout`, a sample aborted mid-generation goes back to the data buffer and is resumed later. `generate()` resumes it with a `max_new_tokens` budget reduced by `sample.response_length` and appends the new tokens after the existing response, so the request must be conditioned on that response.

For samples with images, the request is built as:

```python
payload["image_data"] = [...]
payload["text"] = sample.prompt
```

`sample.prompt` does not include the response generated so far, so SGLang starts a fresh response from the prompt. The new tokens are then appended af

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

## Background

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

Fixes #2409

## Problem

`compute_gpqa_reward` falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply. A reply that never answers, for example `I'm sorry, but I can't help with that.`, therefore scored 1.0 whenever the gold letter (`a`, `b`, `c`) occurred inside a word, and a short numeric choice such as `11` matched inside `2011` or `111`.

## Approach

- A one-character label that is a valid option letter is no longer added t

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

items.body:
## Description

### 1. Colocate weight sync fails on every GPU but 0 (ROCm)

On ROCm a HIP IPC handle carries the **exporter's** device ordinal, and `hipIpcOpenMemHandle`
resolves it in the **importer's** enumeration; CUDA honours the importer's current device instead.

items.summary: Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slimevalidateargs with, because it stat'd args.refload before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.
items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

`_parse_extra_env_vars` split each assignment on every `=` and then kept only the second component. For example:

was parsed as:
